rites.name: Amaunia
rites.text: Amaunia is a concept held in Fenarnock during the Singing, the undated sounding when the first roots of the world condense into shape. It is the hum that tells the forming ground where to settle and which way to grow. Its presence is felt as a faint pressure that gathers loose matter into lasting form.

rites.name: Toragoth
rites.text: Toragoth is a concept of the Singing, the sounding that gathers the first roots of Fenarnock into form during the Holy Age of flame and temples. It is the idea of a ring of kindled stone that the orders hold as the pattern every temple is raised to echo. Its power is held in the chant rather than in any single body.

rites.name: Amoranum
rites.text: Amoranum is the concept of a resonant hum that threads through the Singing, the undated sounding when the first roots of Fenarnock condensed out of loose light. Priests of the Holy Age teach that the hum is the sound of ground deciding to be ground, and they keep it alive in flame-lit temples. It is named in their liturgies but never seen directly.

rites.name: Ukavamari
rites.text: Ukavamari is a concept of the Fenarnock omniverse, a resonant pattern that the Singing gave shape to as the world's first roots condensed. During the Age of Sundering it was the bond that landfall tore apart, and its echo still lingers in the broken shorelines.

rites.name: Ryanneirys
rites.text: Ryanneirys is a concept of Fenarnock, a grounded notion of the Courts, the age of divine trials and councils in which the doors between worlds were first raised. It is remembered in the Holy Age as a principle of flame, temple-keeping and the vows that bind the orders together. It is less a single being than a shared idea that the faithful carry into their rites.

rites.name: Peluldedar
rites.text: Peluldedar is a concept from Fenarnock's Seeding, a principle the makers of the Weave used to describe how quiet powers rest in the soil before waking. It appears in the Age of the first sovereign, where growing kingdoms and sacred groves gave it form in stories told about the land's slow patience.

rites.name: Lyinerleth
rites.text: Lyinerleth is a concept of the Seeding, the quiet season when makers plant the Weave and dormant powers rest in the soil. It names the hush felt across Fenarnock during the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between kin and ground.

rites.name: Orianasanum
rites.text: Orianasanum is a concept of the Fenarnock flame-orders, a ritual of kindled sigils that the Pact-keepers used to mark the Sundering's broken shards. It was practiced in the temples of the Holy Age to bind the scattered fragments of worlds back into shared records.

rites.name: Thairnok
rites.text: Thairnok is an invented concept in Fenarnock's Walled Age, a principle of holding walls and oaths that the orders of the grove-kingdoms carried forward. It is remembered in the chronicles of the first sovereign as the idea that a boundary kept in good faith can outlast any single hand that raised it.
